title: Prediction: Eli Lilly Will Be Worth $2 Trillion by 2031
author: Prosper Junior Bakiny
description: Eli Lilly is positioned to become the first healthcare company to reach a $2 trillion market cap by 2031, requiring a 12.7% compound annual growth rate. The company's GLP-1 drug portfolio, led by tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound), is expected to drive strong revenue growth despite increasing competition. Additional growth catalysts include new product launches like Foundayo, pipeline candidates such as retatrutide, and AI-driven cost efficiencies across the organization.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article presents a bullish case for Eli Lilly, highlighting strong revenue growth prospects driven by its dominant GLP-1 portfolio, promising pipeline candidates, successful recent drug approvals (Kisunla, Omvoh), and AI-driven productivity gains. The company's ability to achieve 12.7% CAGR to reach $2 trillion valuation is deemed achievable, and the current 34x forward earnings multiple is justified given superior growth rates compared to peers.

Novo Nordisk is mentioned only in a 'Read Next' section headline suggesting it has underperformed relative to Eli Lilly in the GLP-1 market, but no substantive analysis is provided in the main article content.
Johnson & Johnson is mentioned only in a 'Read Next' section headline for a comparative analysis article, but receives no analysis or commentary in the main article content.

title: Eli Lilly Stock Has Skyrocketed. Novo Nordisk Has Crashed. 1 Number Explains Why They're Not Even Close Anymore.
author: Matthew Benjamin
description: Eli Lilly has significantly outperformed Novo Nordisk in the booming GLP-1 obesity drug market, with Lilly commanding 60% market share compared to Novo's smaller portion of the combined 87% duopoly. While the obesity drug market is projected to grow from $66 billion in 2025 to $120 billion by 2030, Lilly's stock has surged 58% over 52 weeks, whereas Novo has plummeted 62% since July 2024. However, Novo's recent launch of a pill-form obesity drug could shift the competitive landscape.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Dominant 60% market share in the rapidly growing obesity drug segment, strong stock performance (+58% over 52 weeks, +13.4% YTD), and leading product efficacy with Zepbound driving market leadership.

Despite significant recent stock decline (-62% since July 2024, -5% YTD), the company has positive momentum from its newly launched pill-form Wegovy with strong early uptake and revised higher sales forecasts, suggesting potential competitive recovery.

title: Novo Nordisk provides update on the ZEUS phase 3 trial in people with ASCVD, CKD and inflammation
author: Na
description: Novo Nordisk announced that ziltivekimab failed to meet its primary endpoint in the ZEUS phase 3 trial, showing no significant reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) despite achieving the expected biological effect of IL-6 pathway inhibition. The drug demonstrated a hazard ratio of 0.99 versus placebo in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and inflammation. The company will take a non-cash impairment charge in Q3 2026 but maintains its 2026 profit outlook and plans to continue two additional cardiovascular trials (HERMES and ARTEMIS) expected to report in H1 2027.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company's lead cardiovascular drug candidate failed to demonstrate efficacy in reducing major adverse cardiovascular events despite achieving biological target engagement. This represents a significant clinical and commercial setback, resulting in a non-cash impairment charge. However, the negative impact is partially mitigated by the company's maintained 2026 profit outlook and commitment to continue other cardiovascular trials.

title: Watch Out, Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk: Amgen's Monthly Weight Loss Drug Has 6 Phase 3 Trials Running -- and It's Coming for Your Patients
author: Alex Carchidi
description: Amgen is developing MariTide, a monthly weight loss injection, to compete with Eli Lilly's and Novo Nordisk's weekly GLP-1 drugs. While the monthly dosing offers convenience, MariTide's phase 2 efficacy data don't suggest it will outperform competitors. Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk are advancing newer therapies including oral and combination drugs, positioning them ahead of Amgen in the competitive weight loss market.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Amgen has a potential convenience advantage with monthly dosing, the article emphasizes that MariTide lacks evidence of superior efficacy or tolerability compared to competitors, and major trial results won't arrive until 2027, making it unlikely to capture significant market share before competitors launch superior alternatives.

Eli Lilly is positioned favorably with its oral drug Foundayo already approved and multiple pipeline candidates. The article suggests oral formulations are preferable to injections, and the company doesn't need to fear Amgen's competition in the near term.

Novo Nordisk has filed for approval of CagriSema and maintains a strong market position with multiple weight loss candidates in development. The article indicates the company is well-positioned and doesn't face significant near-term threat from Amgen.

title: Novo Nordisk A/S - share repurchase programme
author: Na
description: Novo Nordisk continues its DKK 15 billion share repurchase programme, having repurchased 25.9 million B shares worth DKK 7.16 billion as of 24 July 2026. The company has also filed a false advertising lawsuit against Eli Lilly over misleading GLP-1 medicine advertising campaigns.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Eli Lilly faces a false advertising lawsuit from Novo Nordisk regarding GLP-1 medicine comparisons, indicating regulatory and legal challenges that could impact brand reputation and market position in the competitive GLP-1 segment.

The share repurchase programme is a routine capital allocation activity indicating confidence in valuation, but the legal action against Eli Lilly suggests competitive pressure and potential reputational concerns in the GLP-1 market. These factors balance to a neutral outlook.
